title: Choose the Page to Hand landing-page structure
question: Same product, proof, and visual system; three different ways to make the value immediately legible.

options.label: Practice Folio
options.thesis: A composed two-page spread pairs the promise with one decisive view of the real practice system.
options.viewport: The left page states the offer and actions; the right page proves it with the app, with the next folio opening visible below.
options.risk: The folio metaphor fails if it becomes decorative instead of making the product easier to understand.

options.label: The Lit Score
options.thesis: The actual practice interface is the hero, surrounded by only the offer, price, and next action.
options.viewport: A large, angled app proof occupies the opening while terse copy and two actions lock to its edges.
options.risk: It can resemble a conventional software hero unless the app proof truly dominates the composition.

options.label: Proof Strip
options.thesis: One continuous reading line shows the full transformation: page, performance, feedback, next practice.
options.viewport: A horizontal proof sequence crosses the first screen, with the promise and actions embedded in the same line.
options.risk: The sequence needs ruthless hierarchy or it will read as a feature diagram instead of a desirable product.
